meta.intro: Today's throughline: AI's physical and political limits are showing, from voter backlash on data centers to Japan's search for state-backed demand.
meta.briefingTitle: METR Finds AI Speeding Up AI, Voters Reject Data Centers, and Japan Tries Government Demand and Cross-Border Capital
meta.summary: The common thread is who funds and permits the build-out. METR's audit says capability growth at Anthropic is running about 1.9x faster, while voters rejected roughly 38 of 41 local data-center measures and chip stocks sold off. Early-stage money keeps flowing to agent plumbing: Battery into construction paperwork, crypto funds into an agent marketplace. Japan answers with state demand (a paid domestic-LLM call from April 2027), a proposed Korea-Japan data-center fund, and a 17-sector priority list, all still small against US private capital.

gaps.label: Sovereign frontier-model pretraining
gaps.note: Unchanged — the Gennai call gives domestic models a buyer from April 2027, but no new pre-training compute or weights were announced this week.

gaps.label: Depth of private risk capital for AI infrastructure
gaps.note: Up one — a Korea-SBI ¥1.15T data-center fund is only under discussion, while US seeds like Shackleton's $5M and Sentra's $150M closed.

gaps.label: Domestic leading-edge chip manufacturing
gaps.note: Unchanged — the 17-sector plan ranks chips first, but no per-sector yen or new fab capacity was disclosed.

gaps.label: Early-stage AI venture formation
gaps.note: Unchanged — MUSE's ¥1.75B is about $11M, versus Cowboy's and Shackleton's $5M seeds that are only the start of US rounds.

items.headline: METR Audit Inside Anthropic Finds Capability Growth About 1.9x Faster Since Oct 2025, With Faster Compute Ruled Out as the Cause
items.dek: The first outside, quantified read on AI speeding up AI research comes with a cancelled compute check attached.

analysis.happening: METR (about 2.5 FTE, Aug 12 to Oct 29) used Anthropic's AECI index and estimated 1.9x faster growth since Oct 2025 (95% CI 1.5-2.8x). It ruled out faster training-compute growth as the driver, pointing to AI-assisted R&D instead.
analysis.now: If real, roadmaps compress faster than planning assumes. Caveats: AECI favors well-specified, easily graded tasks, redactions limit checking, and METR says Anthropic cancelled a planned compute-allocation check. One summary's ~80% attribution to AI use is not confirmed in METR's text.
analysis.future: Watch for replications at OpenAI or Google, Anthropic's answer on the cancelled audit, and whether AECI gains show up in real-world agent task benchmarks.

items.headline: Voters Rejected Data Centers in About 38 of 41 Local Ballot Measures, and AI Chip Stocks Sold Off
items.dek: The midterms turned data-center siting into a market risk, and governors in four big hosting states may tighten rules.

analysis.happening: Ballotpedia tracked 41 data-center ballot measures in 10 states; Fast Company reports voters chose to ban or pause local development in 38, with 3 unreported. Ohio had 21. Digitimes says Texas, Ohio, Georgia and Pennsylvania could tighten controls. AI and chip stocks fell Nov 5-6.
analysis.now: Local permitting, not chip supply, may set US capacity adds; likely delay of orders rather than cancellations, and no customer cancellations are shown. Caveat: tallies differ by outlet (38 of 40+ across 13 states per one, 38 of 47 per another) and Digitimes is paywalled.
analysis.future: Watch state moratorium bills, Nvidia's next guide, and whether developers shift to friendlier states or onsite power. Non-US build-outs, including Japan, could benefit.

items.headline: New York's Shackleton AI Exits Stealth With a $5M Seed From Battery Ventures to Run Construction Paperwork With Agents
items.dek: The founders built the agent OS for their own contracting business first, then took it to market.

analysis.happening: Shackleton AI emerged Nov 4 with a $5M seed led by Battery Ventures, joined by Brick & Mortar, Trust Ventures, Correlation Ventures, Motivate Partners and Thayer. One source says the platform manages over $1B in project value across 15+ states.
analysis.now: Battery's thesis, per partner Michael Brown, is that construction is among the economy's largest, least-digitized sectors; dogfooding is the edge. Caveat: the founder revenue claim ($35M for contractor Ernest) comes from a single source.
analysis.future: Look for vertical agent plays in other paperwork-heavy trades (permitting, subcontractor compliance) and a Series A within 12-18 months proving non-founder customers.

items.headline: Cowboy Launches an 'App Store for AI Agents' With a $5M Seed From Anagram, Compound and Nebular
items.dek: A New York incubation from ex-Snap founders' fund Uncommon Projects opens with 100+ agents and 10,000 data feeds.

analysis.happening: Cowboy raised a $5M seed from Nebular, Compound, Semantic Ventures, Anagram, Shine Ventures and Uncommon Projects, plus angels including Kevin Kwok. CEO Chad DePue is ex-Snap and Uniswap. Its General Store launched with 100+ agents and 10,000 data feeds, each hire in an isolated sandbox.
analysis.now: Crypto-native funds backing agent distribution bets that agents need marketplaces and payment rails, not just models. Caveat: the Cowboy Chain payments network is testnet only, and a two-sided marketplace faces cold-start risk on a thin $5M.
analysis.future: Track paid usage versus the 100-agent launch count and whether mainnet ships late 2026. Niche agents and data feeds are an early monetization path for builders.

items.headline: Glasshand Tops Product Hunt by Renting Real iPhones and Macs to Coding Agents
items.dek: A hosted service gives Claude Code or Codex a real device with eSIM, while open-source local rivals already exist.

analysis.happening: Glasshand led Product Hunt's Nov 5 leaderboard (score 384, 80 comments) over Rerun (273) and Living Brain (253). The maker says real iPhones and Macs, not emulators; billing is for the hosted device even with your own Claude account. Local alternatives: Zeptap and open-source Phone Harness.
analysis.now: Mobile app testing by agents without an API is the gap. Caveat: comments raise unanswered questions on App Store sign-in without sharing passwords and on device models; pricing is unclear, and local tools undercut hosted cost.
analysis.future: Watch whether device-farm incumbents add agent APIs, and whether eSIM/SMS handling raises abuse and ToS issues.

items.headline: MUSE Raises ¥1.75B for 'Armo' Store Robots, With US Launch and Mass Production Next
items.dek: A Japanese retail-robot startup takes its shelf-restocking robot to the US, reversing the usual direction.

analysis.happening: MUSE announced ¥1.75B (about $11M, our conversion) on Nov 5; Nikkei lists equity plus loans. It targets 50% overseas sales within three years. Funds go to mass production, AI upgrades and US entry. The prior round was ¥570M in June 2024.
analysis.now: Versus the US: American robotics money mostly goes to warehouses, while Japan's labor shortage and dense stores favor in-store robots. Caveat: lead investors for this round are unconfirmed, and 'physical AI' is Nikkei's label.
analysis.future: A named US retail pilot and Armo's unit price are the real validation; watch if Incubate Fund and XTech, backers of the 2024 round, follow on.

items.headline: Korea Investment and SBI Discuss a ¥1.15T Fund for AI Data Centers in Japan
items.dek: Korean and Japanese financial groups want to pool money for a Stargate-style Japanese buildout.

analysis.happening: KED Global reports Korea Investment Holdings and SBI Holdings are discussing a joint fund: headline 10T won, subtitle an initial ¥1.15T target expanding over 30 years. Hankyung gives the same first-phase figure; another Korean report says at least ¥1T. The structure is compared to Stargate.
analysis.now: Versus the US: American data centers run on hyperscaler capex and private credit; Japan is trying a cross-border bank and brokerage pool. Caveat: only 'in discussion', sizes conflict, and no SBI primary release was found.
analysis.future: Watch for a signed MOU, anchor tenants, the site (Hokkaido and Kyushu are tagged) and power procurement. The Nov 6 chip selloff could slow commitments.

items.headline: Japan's Digital Agency Plans a Paid FY2027 Call for Domestic LLMs, With the Test Growing to 300 Questions
items.dek: A guaranteed government buyer for domestic models from April 2027 is a rare demand-side lever.

analysis.happening: The Gennai program tested 7 domestic models, 5 contracted: tsuzumi 2, Sarashina3 mini, cotomi v3, Takane 32B, PLaMo 2.0 Prime. The FY2027 call is planned for Nov with a Dec deadline and paid use from April 2027. Tests grow from 50 to 300 questions with mandatory tool-use; about 180,000 civil servants are in the pilot.
analysis.now: Versus the US: no single central buying channel exists for one domestic model class; Japan gives sovereign models a government customer. Caveat: the Nov start comes from a secondary Oct 21 article and I found no official call document.
analysis.future: Check digital.go.jp for the call, watch who applies (ELYZA and CC Gov-LLM dropped out in 2026), and the Gennai 2.0 agent release around Feb 2027.

items.headline: Japan's Growth Strategy Narrows to 17 Sectors, With AI Data Centers and Chips First
items.dek: The government moves from a broad wish list to prioritized, funded sectors.

analysis.happening: Nikkei Asia (Nov 6) says Japan will fund 17 strategic sectors, with cloud and AI data centers prioritized, chips near-term and AI medium-term. A June draft put public and private investment above ¥370T through FY2040, chips largest at ¥68T and data centers ¥32.7T through FY2035.
analysis.now: Versus the US: American capex is private, while Japan sets a public-private target list. Caveat: the Nov 6 text gave no per-sector funding, and the June figures are a draft roadmap with the government share unspecified.
analysis.future: Watch the FY2027 budget request in December for actual yen per sector, and who gets data-center subsidies. Startups should check for subsidy windows.
